description: Run the regular DuckDB test suite over a quack client/server connection. on_init starts a quack server inside the test instance and attaches back to it over TCP; on_new_connection makes that remote catalog the default database, so every statement of every test travels through the quack RPC protocol.
comment: Uses a fixed port (9494), so only one unittest process may use this config at a time; scripts/run_duckdb_tests.py rewrites the port per worker for --jobs. on_cleanup stops the server on purpose: server-side connections hold a strong reference to the DatabaseInstance that owns the server, so without the explicit stop the instance (and its whole task scheduler) is never reclaimed. settings.async_threads keeps what does still leak (instances abandoned by restart/load) cheap.
on_init: CALL quack_stop('quack:localhost:9494'); CALL quack_serve('quack:localhost:9494', token='quack_test_token'); CREATE OR REPLACE SECRET __quack_test_secret (TYPE quack, TOKEN 'quack_test_token'); ATTACH IF NOT EXISTS 'quack:localhost:9494' AS quack_remote;
skip_error_messages: Vacuum is only implemented for DuckDB tables
Multiple streaming scans or streaming scans + CTAS / insert in the same query

skip_tests.reason: Only the error message crosses the wire, not the exception type (ErrorResponse serializes error.RawMessage() only), so the right error arrives as an 'Invalid Input Error'

Client-side 'syntax error at or near "."' - a qualified name is rendered with an empty component during the catalog reload that follows ALTER + DROP. The most common case of the lossy deparse below, and counted separately because the trigger is understood

The client re-serializes the parsed statement back to SQL text before sending it, and the deparse is lossy: lambdas come out as the deprecated -> arrow, NULL::TYPE loses its cast, and literals of extension types are emitted unquoted, so the server rejects the text
A remote query whose result has duplicate column names cannot be bound: table "quack_query_by_name" has duplicate column name
ATTACH fails outright: a remote table cannot be bound while the client builds the catalog (Failed to bind remote table while attaching quack catalog)
Prepared statement parameters do not reach the server: 'Values were not provided for the following parameters'
The client abandons an in-flight request: 'superseded by a new query'
Transaction semantics differ over the wire - most of these are 'cannot start a transaction within a transaction', the rest aborted-transaction state and COMMIT/ROLLBACK with no active transaction
Feature not implemented in the quack storage extension yet
The quack client catalog only exposes tables and views: sequences, types, indexes, macros and functions created through the connection are not visible to the client binder
The test collides with the config's own on_init rather than with quack itself: it changes secret manager settings, or re-runs on_init against a server that is already serving
A statement expected to fail succeeds over the quack connection
The remote error text differs from what the test expects, beyond the exception type
A statement that should succeed fails with a remote error not yet grouped further
EXPLAIN / plan inspection: every base table lives behind a remote quack scan, so the local plan is replaced by a single 'Quack Query By Name' node and the expected operators never appear
Result differs: catalog and metadata queries (SHOW, duckdb_* tables, information_schema, pg_catalog, comments) describe the quack catalog rather than a local DuckDB one
Returns a different result over a quack connection, for a reason not yet grouped
